newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Thousands at burial of Nigeria's first president.
newsitem.headline: Thousands at burial of Nigeria's first president.

text.p: Nigeria finally buried its first president, Nnamdi Azikiwe, on Saturday after a series of funeral ceremonies following his death six months ago.

State radio, reporting live from the ceremony said thousands of people, the largest crowd ever seen in the sprawling city of Onitsha, watched as his body was lowered into its final resting place in his Inosi Onira Retreat.
"Zik of Africa," as he was known, died six months ago and would have turned 92 years old on Saturday.

Dignitaries from all over the nation were present at the final ceremony, a mixture of traditional and religious rituals beginning with the killing of a giant cow in the full view of the crowd as is customary for someone of Azikiwe's stature.
A Christian service followed and then came eulogies from Nigerian military and political leaders.
"Zik was a man of the people who embraced people from all tribes and creed," said Lieutenant-General Oladipo Diya, the second in command in Nigeria's military government.

Azikiwe's body had been on tour of Nigeria all week. It was taken round by an airforce plane first to Zungeru in the north where he was born in 1904 for childhood friends to pay him their last respects.

On Tuesday it was displayed in the federal capital Abuja where military ruler General Sani Abacha presided over a lying-in-state ceremony attended by the presidents of Sierra Leone, Guinea and Equitarial Guinea.
A chief in his native Iboland holding the title Owelle of Onitsha, Azikiwe was considered non-partisan in a multi-ethnic nation which tribal tensions have frequently threatened to tear apart.
Azikiwe became president in 1963 when Nigeria was founded as a republic after independence from Britain in 1960. He remained until the first military coup in 1966.

The politician, scholar, poet and journalist helped to end the Biafran civil war that had plunged his Ibo people into mass suffering when he returned to the federal side after seeing the hopelessness of the war that killed a million people.
